title: Trim transitive Node deps and introduce CI dependency viability gate
author: Evelyn Chen
description: Background: our monorepo has accumulated a number of transitive Node dependencies that inflate install times, increase CI image size, and surface sporadic supply-chain noise (native bindings, archived tarballs). Motivation: reduce developer iteration friction and CI flakiness by pruning unused transitive packages, surface risky packages earlier, and add an automated 'viability' gate in CI so new/updated dependencies are verified before they reach main. What this PR does: 1) Introduces a lightweight CI action (ci/.github/actions/dependency-viability) that performs three fast checks for a candidate dependency: license policy, artifact surface check (are binaries available for current platforms), and a smoke import + tiny runtime invocation against a constrained test harness. The action is intentionally conservative (fast heuristics, not full fuzzing) and fails fast when a dependency appears unviable. 2) Adds a dep-pruning script (tools/dep-prune/prune-transitives.sh) which leverages the project dep-graph to suggest a minimal removal set of transitive packages. The script produces a report and a provisional package.json patch that can be reviewed. 3) Applies the automated pruning suggestions in a controlled set of workspace packages (packages/sdk-node, packages/cli, examples/web) after manual verification. 4) Updates CI workflows to gate PRs that add or bump top-level direct dependencies to run the dependency-viability check; workflow defaults are set to run the gate only for dependency changes to keep runtime low. Migration notes / developer impact: - Local installs may show a reduced node_modules footprint; run `yarn rebuild` in workspaces with native deps. - If you rely on an overly permissive transitive API, you may need to pin a direct dependency; the prune report contains quick remediation recommendations. Testing performed: - Unit and integration suites for impacted packages. - End-to-end smoke runs in a small matrix (linux/mac node16). - Manual verification of binary availability for node-sass-like packages. Rollout plan: - Merge to main guarded by a short feature flag in CI so we can disable the gate quickly if we see false positives. - Monitor dep-gate failures and revert to a whitelist approach if needed. Risks & mitigations: false positives from the artifact surface check can block PRs; mitigated by an explicit bypass label (ci/deps-bypass) and a fast manual triage playbook. Supply-chain risk reduced by earlier failure surface. Related work: references ENG-1329 for dependency hygiene initiative and ENG-1401 for CI runtime optimizations. Checklist: [x] unit tests updated [x] smoke matrix added [x] docs (docs/engineering/dependency-guidelines.md) updated [x] release notes added

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Can the artifact surface check be extended to validate prebuilt .node artifacts are not from deprecated platforms? If not, how do we avoid a false positive for arm64-only packages?

Evelyn Chen: Currently we validate available tarballs and check node-pre-gyp manifest entries; for arm64-only we surface a warning and allow bypass via ci/deps-bypass label. We can add more platform heuristics later.
Samir Khatri: CI runtime looks sane but we should avoid running the gate for non-dep changes to keep queue time low.
Evelyn Chen: Gate is scoped in the workflow to files matching package.json and yarn.lock changes only.
Priya Verma: Please add a short note in the contributor guide explaining how to bypass and when to request whitelist inclusion.
Evelyn Chen: Added docs/engineering/dependency-guidelines.md and a short bypass playbook in that file.

release_notes: Introduce CI dependency viability gate and prune unused transitive Node deps to reduce CI image size and surface supply-chain issues earlier. No breaking changes expected; developers may need to pin direct deps if a previously implicit transitive API was relied on.
notes_for_ops: Enable the ci gating feature flag in the CI control plane after merge. Monitor failures during the first 48 hours and watch for recurring bypass label usage.
post_merge_actions: Triage any ci/deps-bypass uses and add whitelist entries if necessary
Run a repo-wide dep-graph analysis monthly
